Underwater segmentation with 6,000 training images

SegFormer-B0 trained on 3,000 SynTIDE image–mask pairs and 3,000 human-labeled UIIS pairs, compared with the three original training conditions.

What changed with twice the data?

The expanded mix reached 48.54% six-class mean IoU on the 691-image UIIS holdout. Doubling the original balanced mix changed this score by +1.76 percentage points (paired 95% interval −2.38 to +4.37).

Compared with training on the same 3,000 real images alone, the change was −0.76 percentage points (paired 95% interval −5.12 to +2.70). Both UIIS intervals include zero, so the sampled test groups leave the direction of either change uncertain.

Effects across test sets

Doubling the mixed pool changed DeepFish fish IoU from 53.41% to 56.49%, a difference of +3.08 percentage points (paired 95% interval +0.97 to +5.84). On CoralscapesV2, the expanded mix scored 4.91% compared with 6.12% for real-only training. The figure shows paired differences at the same training budget. Zero marks equal performance.

The paired bootstrap draws resample 649 UIIS visual groups, 49 DeepFish recording groups, or five CoralscapesV2 sites, with 2,000 draws per test set. Resampling the 19 DeepFish habitats gives a 95% interval of −0.55 to +8.73 points for the expanded mix versus real only. Five sites give limited information about performance on new reefs.

Generator-source overlap

Of the 691 UIIS holdout images, 578 closely matched photographs listed in TIDE generator training, including 56 identical files. Across all 14,573 indexed source photos, the screen found zero matches in either external test. The 113 UIIS images without a detected match yield an expanded-minus-real difference of −2.47 percentage points (paired 95% interval −6.85 to +2.08). They include only one robot image and three wreck images. Of 2,000 draws, 1,222 contained all six reference classes.

The narrower screen against the original UIIS training source alone retained 342 images and yielded an expanded-minus-real difference of +0.28 percentage points (paired 95% interval −5.74 to +4.24). Downstream training excluded candidate photos in groups matching the holdouts. The generator-source screen is a separate check on upstream exposure and can miss strongly transformed copies. Examples from all four models

What the comparisons measure

Expanded mix versus original mix. The expanded pool contains all 3,000 images used by the smaller mix plus 1,500 additional images from each source. Both conditions presented 16,000 real and 16,000 synthetic images per run, with four from each source per batch. The same 32,000 presentations cover 5.33 passes through the expanded pool and 10.67 passes through the smaller one. This measures the benefit of greater training diversity at fixed compute for these selected pools. An equal-epoch comparison would require additional updates.

Expanded mix versus real only. Both conditions have exactly the same 3,000 human-labeled images. The expanded condition adds 3,000 synthetic pairs while reducing presentations of the real images from 32,000 to 16,000 per run. Its result reflects both changes. Over one complete pass through the expanded pool, synthetic images contribute 56.79% of supervised pixels after padding and ignored pixels are excluded. The real pool contains 2,225 inferred visual groups. Each synthetic image comes from a different caption.

Every model used the same ImageNet-pretrained MiT-B0 encoder, newly initialized seven-class segmentation head, seeds 17, 29 and 43, and 4,000 AdamW updates with batches of eight. Inputs were fit and padded to 512 × 512. The shared recipe used flips and brightness augmentation, a 100-step warm-up, and linear learning-rate decay. Final checkpoints were evaluated after cropping the padding and restoring logits to the original mask size before class assignment.

Metrics pool valid pixel counts over each test set before averaging run scores. Background contributes false positives to foreground classes. Label 255 is excluded. Bootstrap draws resample the same test groups for all arms and seeds. Intervals quantify test-group sampling uncertainty conditional on these fitted models and training pools. Seed variation is reported separately. UIIS six-class draws require all six reference classes.
